business_problem: Pronto Software needed to keep delivering analytics and newer AI-driven capabilities to mid-market ERP customers without forcing them to assemble separate BI teams or absorb the complexity usually associated with enterprise analytics tools.
solution_summary: Pronto Software extended its long-running IBM partnership by embedding IBM Cognos Analytics deeply inside Pronto Xi and then using IBM-led co-innovation to map new AI use cases into the ERP platform. Cognos became the reporting and analytics layer inside Pronto Xi, packaged so mid-market customers could access decision-support capabilities without standing up dedicated BI organizations. The partnership also runs as an engineering loop: Pronto's product teams discuss roadmap options with IBM R&D, use Pronto Xi as a beta platform for selected new functionality, and test how innovations land in real customer workflows. More recently, IBM provided AI training and a hackathon, followed by IBM Garage design thinking, to prioritize use cases such as maintenance-service scheduling and define MVPs based on underlying ERP data flows, integrations, and UX changes. The result is a pragmatic architecture that combines embedded analytics today with a structured path to AI-enabled automation tomorrow.

solution_components.name: Pronto Xi
solution_components.role: Acts as the ERP platform in which analytics and future AI automation use cases are embedded for mid-market customers.

solution_components.name: IBM Cognos Analytics

data_flow: Operational data inside Pronto Xi feeds embedded Cognos reporting and analytics for end customers, while the same ERP workflows and data context are used to design and test future AI use cases such as scheduling optimization.
business_outcome: Pronto made advanced analytics more consumable for a broad mid-market ERP base and created a disciplined roadmap for adding AI-powered automation features that can deliver faster time to value for customers.
